newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-HART WORRIED ABOUT ENGLISH RUGBY CIVIL WAR.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-HART WORRIED ABOUT ENGLISH RUGBY CIVIL WAR.

text.p: All Black coach John Hart expressed concern on Wednesday over the civil war in English rugby that threatens to undermine the first of two matches the New Zealand Barbarians are playing on their short tour.

The current impasse between the Rugby Football Union and the English Professional Rugby Clubs has led to players from the top two divisions in England being withheld from playing in divisional matches.

That means that when the Barbarians play the North at Huddersfield on Sunday, they will be facing a team made up principally of players from third and fourth divisions. Hardly a good rehearsal for the Twickenham sell-out against England on November 30
It is a problem which is also affecting Argentina, Queensland and South Africa A who are all currently touring Britain.
"For us it is a forerunner to the game against England the following Saturday and we would obviously like to have the strongest opposition possible," said Hart.
"It's disappointing -- but then it may be more disappointing for them than for us."
Hart warned the two warring factions in the battle for control of the game in England over the perils for English rugby of continuing the dispute.

"The dispute between the clubs and the union is one which obviously needs to be resolved. One thing that was shown in the southern hemisphere this year was that decisions needed to be made quickly for the good of the game.

"The longer you leave these decisions, the greater the divide becomes, the personalities take over and the game suffers. One can only hope that common sense prevails and agreement is reached very quickly."
On a brighter note, Hart stressed that his touring side were intent on running the ball in the best Barbarians fashion although he did stress that the game against England was not a "test".
"How we might see it and how England might see it may be different," he said. "It is certainly not a test as far as we are concerned but obviously it will be played in a true test spirit.
"We want to take the ball and run in the Barbarian tradition and that's why we have brought some of our most exciting young players.
"I hope England do the same because that would be great for world rugby, to see two sides from the northern and southern hemispheres playing the game as it's meant to be played.

"And I think the new rules have created opportunities for the game to be played positively -- if both sides want to do that. If one side doesn't, then you can still destroy it but I am hoping England will be positive. Boy, they've got the talent to be."

Coming on the back of a tough season which saw the All Blacks gain their first ever series win in South Africa and play 10 tests in 13 weeks, the Barbarians' selectors have left behind some familiar faces such as Zinzan Brooke, Walter Little and Frank Bunce. But it is still a strong team.

Led by All Blacks' captain Sean Fitzpatrick, the 24-man Barbarians squad contains 15 men who have played test rugby for New Zealand, including giant wing Jonah Lomu, veteran flanker Michael Jones, locks Ian Jones and Robin Brooke, prop Olo Brown, fly-half Andrew Mehrtens and full-back Christian Cullen.
They can also call on Lomu's provincial teammate, Joelli Vidiri who played eight tests for Fiji before joining the lengthy South Seas queue for an All Black cap.

That experience, however, has been blended with youth, which sees half the side aged under 22, and inexperience as Hart tests a few of the players who may come into the reckoning for the 1999 World Cup in Wales. For example, 21-year-old scrumhalf Mark Robinson has played just eight provincial games for North Harbour.

Fitzpatrick, for one, will be more than anxious to win the game against England for although the All Blacks destroyed Will Carling's team in the World Cup semifinal last year and have since gone on to prove themselves the best side in the world, the feisty hooker still remembers the defeat when he last time he played at Twickenham in 1993.
"My memories of Twickenham are not too good, we were well beaten by England," he said. "It's been a long season for us but we are not going to let ourselves down in the last two games."
